elements.element: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No right of first refusal / match-or-disclose mechanic operating as de facto exclusivity on Customer
elements.evidence: mandatory "must disclose and match" replaced with "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: Any exclusivity confined to a defined product category
elements.evidence: condition absent: no exclusivity obligation remains after "is not required to disclose or match"
condition absent: no exclusivity period is imposed on Customer in 7.2

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates
elements.evidence: condition absent: nothing to terminate, as clause imposes no exclusivity

reasons: The single replacement converts the mandatory disclose-and-match duty into an express negation, eliminating the de facto right of first refusal and satisfying the preferred position of no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer.
Change is confined to the operative verb phrase ('Customer must disclose and match' → 'Customer is not required to disclose or match'); no new exceptions, defined terms, or boilerplate added.
Fallback constraints are trivially satisfied because no exclusivity obligation survives; no exclusivity was invented to meet them.

Minor drafting artefact: the retained lead-in 'Before engaging another provider' now reads oddly against a negative duty, but it introduces no contradiction or dangling mechanic and is consistent with Section 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement.
